newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges police to keep order at HK handover.
newsitem.headline: China urges police to keep order at HK handover.

text.p: China's top policeman has ordered cops in the capital to redouble efforts to thwart public disturbances ahead of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1, the Legal Daily said on Thursday.
Minister of Public Security Tao Siju had met organisers of handover celebrations in Beijing and called on the capital's police force to make greater efforts to maintain stability, the newspaper said.

"The Beijing Public Security Bureau... should ensure the celebrations go off without a hitch and at the same time fully uphold the order of all celebratory activities," the newspaper quoted Tao as saying.
Beijing has billed the resumption of Chinese sovereignty over Hong Kong after more than 150 years of British colonial rule as one of the most important events of the year, if not the century.

Chinese authorities are eager to ensure nothing mars the run-up to the handover at midnight on June 30 and have ordered tighter security around the capital and put troops on alert in restive areas such as the mostly Moslem region of Xinjiang.
In February, a string of bus bombs exploded in the Xinjiang capital Urumqi, killing nine people in attacks coinciding with funeral rites for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping in Beijing.

A homemade bomb also blew up aboard a Beijing bus during a session of China's National People's Congress, or parliament, in March, and in May a man committed suicide in the capital by blowing himself up in a central public park.
